title: OpenAI Responses API Request Workflow
summary: Send a bounded OpenAI Responses API request with environment-based credentials, explicit configuration, typed output inspection, and recoverable failure handling.
prerequisites: An OpenAI API key stored outside source control

sections.title: What you will learn
paragraphs: You will prepare an OpenAI Responses API request, inspect raw REST data by type, and classify failures without exposing credentials. The required lab is offline and deterministic. It needs Node.js 22 and PowerShell 7, but it needs no network, API key, model access, or provider account.

The lab deliberately starts at 6 of 9 passing cases. You will repair only learner.mjs, rerun the same fixtures and tests, and apply the rule to a changed input. The separate reference.mjs illustrates the intended classifier but is never imported by tests.mjs. Synthetic fixture results demonstrate local program behavior, not live API behavior or model quality.

code.label: learning contract
code.code:
Required path: offline fixtures -> failing baseline -> learner repair -> unchanged tests -> changed input
Optional path: environment credentials -> bounded REST request -> typed classification
Never use fixture output as a live API receipt.

sections.title: Prepare the request boundary
paragraphs: The verified REST endpoint is POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses. The JSON body requires model and input, while max_output_tokens can bound generated output. When an application supplies behavioral guidance and user data, keep the guidance in instructions and the user data in input. Authentication uses an Authorization header containing Bearer followed by OPENAI_API_KEY.

For the optional request, choose an available model through PROJECT42_OPENAI_MODEL. This lesson does not identify an available model or make pricing claims. Use only approved, non-secret input. Decide the timeout, output budget, accepted lifecycle states, logging policy, and application validation before transmitting data. The API key must remain in the environment or an approved secret manager and must never enter source code, prompts, or console output.

code.label: request boundary template

sections.title: Follow a filled task, request, and response example
paragraphs: The task below asks for one sentence about approved text. The request separates the stable instruction from the user-supplied note and includes an output budget. The response is an independently authored synthetic object. It is shaped like the fields this lesson consumes, but it is not a captured provider response.

The first output item is reasoning rather than a message. Positional code such as output[0].content[0].text would therefore fail. Typed traversal skips that item, selects the message, then selects its output_text block. The extracted candidate is still untrusted and requires application review. Token figures are intentionally absent because no live measurement established them.

code.label: synthetic worked example

sections.title: Read raw REST data by type
paragraphs: A raw Responses API result includes fields such as id, status, and output. The output array can contain typed reasoning, message, and tool-call items. A message contains a content array whose blocks can include output_text or refusal. Select by these type fields rather than assuming that the first output item and first content block contain text.

The output_text convenience property used by some SDKs is not part of the raw REST shape taught here. The optional program therefore walks body.output itself. This lesson uses completed, incomplete, failed, in_progress, queued, and cancelled as its accepted lifecycle domain. It does not claim that the cited text guide provides a complete formal response schema. A refusal is represented by a typed content block, not by invented refused or error lifecycle values.

code.label: classification precedence
code.code:
1. Reject malformed HTTP metadata or an unknown lifecycle value.
2. Treat a non-2xx HTTP result or failed lifecycle as failed.
3. Classify in_progress or queued as pending, and cancelled as cancelled.
4. Classify incomplete as incomplete, even if partial output_text exists.
5. For completed output, let any refusal block override text.
6. Otherwise join every string-valued output_text block in traversal order.
7. A valid completion without text or refusal is empty.

sections.title: Send a minimal Responses request
paragraphs: This optional Node.js 22 program uses built-in fetch, environment credentials, an environment-selected model, max_output_tokens, and AbortSignal.timeout. It reads JSON before interpreting provider fields, distinguishes the HTTP result from the response lifecycle, and scans typed content. A timeout bounds how long this client waits, but it does not prove that the provider did not receive or process the request.

The program never prints the key, request body, generated text, refusal text, or provider error.message. It emits only a whitelisted diagnostic summary. It reads x-request-id if present without claiming that the header is guaranteed. Running it requires network access, a permitted account, and a model valid for that account. None is required for the offline lab.

code.label: optional-live-request.mjs

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Keep three layers separate. HTTP status reports request transport success or failure. The response status reports lifecycle state. Typed content can report refusal inside an otherwise completed response. Accept candidate text only after all three layers pass and after domain checks confirm that the text is safe, relevant, and permitted for its intended use.

Authentication and invalid-input failures require correction rather than blind retry. For a transient failure, retry only when provider guidance and the operation's side-effect policy permit it, using bounded attempts and backoff. Never expose an authorization header or provider error text in diagnostics. Preserve only approved metadata. After timeout, incomplete, refusal, failure, malformed data, or failed validation, discard the candidate and retain the last verified application state.

Correct authentication and invalid-request failures instead of retrying. Retry only classified transient failures with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, and preserve operation identity. This read-only example has no external side effect, so rollback means discard the unaccepted response and restore the last verified application state. Add idempotency and tested compensation before connecting output to mutations.

code.label: safe verification record
code.code:
Allowed diagnostic fields:
httpStatus: validated integer
requestIdPresent: boolean
responseIdPresent: boolean
responseStatus: validated lifecycle value or unknown
outcome: whitelisted local classification
outputTextBlockCount: nonnegative integer

Do not print:
API keys or authorization headers
provider error.message
sensitive request input
refusal text
unreviewed generated text

sections.title: Create the complete offline lab
paragraphs: Save the following executable PowerShell 7 content as setup.ps1 in a new working location. Run it from that location. It refuses to overwrite project42-responses-lab, then creates learner.mjs, fixtures.mjs, tests.mjs, reference.mjs, and changed-input.mjs. The core exercise performs no network operation and reads no credentials.

Treat fixtures.mjs and tests.mjs as immutable assessment files. The tests independently check each fixture's lifecycle domain and integer HTTP status, invoke the learner function for every case, compare tagged results with deep equality, and gather all failures. Exceptions become explicit threw results instead of being converted to empty strings. Tests import learner.mjs only, never reference.mjs.

code.label: setup.ps1

sections.title: Observe the deliberate 6 of 9 baseline
paragraphs: Run setup.ps1 from its parent directory, enter the generated directory, and run tests.mjs. The exact expected transcript below follows from the supplied synthetic files. The process exits with code 1 because three cases fail. A different transcript means the files, runtime, or command differs from this lab.

The starter already validates the HTTP status integer and lifecycle domain. Its meaningful defect is content-state handling: it treats mixed refusal and text as text, exposes partial incomplete text as completed text, and treats a refusal-only completion as empty. Six successful cases show why a partial pass is not proof that the parser is safe.

sections.title: Interpret the baseline result
paragraphs: This transcript is deterministic fixture evidence, not a live execution receipt. The three failures identify one bounded repair: apply lifecycle and refusal precedence before returning text. Do not edit fixtures.mjs, tests.mjs, reference.mjs, or expected values. Do not substitute the reference function for the learner implementation.

code.label: exact expected baseline output

sections.title: Repair lifecycle and typed-content precedence
paragraphs: Replace only learner.mjs with the code below. The repaired classifier retains HTTP and lifecycle validation, rejects malformed arrays, and keeps pending, cancelled, failed, and incomplete states distinct. For completed responses, it walks all messages and content blocks. If any refusal block appears, refusal overrides every text block. Otherwise, all string-valued output_text blocks are joined in traversal order.

This repair classifies wire data. It does not prove that extracted text is true, safe, complete, or suitable for a decision. Keep those checks in a later application-validation boundary. The separate reference implementation remains a study aid and is not called by the tests.

code.label: replacement learner.mjs

sections.title: Rerun the immutable tests
paragraphs: After replacing only learner.mjs, rerun the unchanged tests. All nine synthetic cases should pass and Node should exit with code 0. This proves only that the learner classifier satisfies the fixture contract. It does not establish provider availability, the complete provider schema, live request success, or generated-output quality.

sections.title: Confirm the repaired result
paragraphs: The exact expected transcript records every case instead of stopping at the first failure. A mismatch is a failed assessment even if the final count was changed manually. Restore tests.mjs and fixtures.mjs from a newly generated lab if either assessment file was edited.

code.label: exact expected repaired output

sections.title: Apply the rule to changed input
paragraphs: Before running changed-input.mjs, predict its tagged result. The changed object contains a reasoning item and two message items with three output_text blocks. It contains no refusal and has completed status with HTTP 200. The answer is {"kind":"text","text":"First Second Third"} because typed traversal ignores reasoning, visits both messages, preserves block order, and joins all three strings with one space.

Run the command below after the repaired tests pass. This assessment imports the learner implementation directly and does not modify an immutable fixture. A first-block parser would return only First. A first-message parser would return First Second. The repaired traversal returns all three values.

sections.title: Recover safely and transfer to an optional real request
paragraphs: The exact changed-input output is PASS changed-input: {"kind":"text","text":"First Second Third"}, followed by exit code 0. This demonstrates transfer to a new local shape. It remains synthetic evidence. To transfer to the optional real request, keep the same sequence: validate HTTP metadata, validate lifecycle, validate arrays, inspect discriminating type fields, give refusal precedence, and send candidate text to application review.

On timeout, stop waiting and record only approved metadata. On authentication or invalid-input failure, correct credentials or payload instead of retrying unchanged. On incomplete, failed, cancelled, refusal, malformed, or unknown data, do not present partial or refusal content as an answer. For queued or in_progress, follow a separately approved retrieval policy. The complete official enum and full output schema were not established by the supplied cited guide, so reverify those details before production deployment.

code.label: evidence boundary and recovery table
code.code:
Offline 9/9 = learner classifier matches authored fixtures
Changed-input pass = classifier transfers to one new authored object
Neither result = live provider execution or model-quality evidence

candidate-text: continue to application validation
refused: stop and report refusal classification
incomplete: stop and report incomplete classification
failed or HTTP failure: retain redacted metadata and diagnose
pending: use an approved follow-up policy
cancelled, invalid, or unknown: reject as non-final

sections.title: Sources and known limits
paragraphs: OpenAI's text-generation guide supports the endpoint, model and input fields, optional output budgeting, instruction separation, and typed traversal of raw output. The quickstart supports environment-based bearer authentication. The error guide supports distinguishing correctable request problems from failures that may warrant controlled retry. Node.js documentation supports AbortSignal.timeout for bounded waiting.

The supplied research did not establish a complete formal schema for every output item, every content subtype, or every lifecycle value. It also did not establish a first-party guarantee for the x-request-id header. The code therefore reads that header only if present and identifies its lifecycle set as this lab's accepted domain. No SDK syntax, model availability, price, live receipt, or quality measurement is claimed.

code.label: verification scope
code.code:
Verified source claims: endpoint, request fields, bearer environment credential pattern,
typed raw output traversal, error-handling distinction, bounded AbortSignal timeout.

Not established here: complete response schema, guaranteed x-request-id header,
model availability, pricing, latency, live output, or model quality.
